newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close mixed in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close mixed in listless trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed mixed on Saturday in slow trade amid a lack of market-moving factors to signal new market direction, brokers said.
The weighted index closed little changed, rising a mere 1.12 points or 0.02 percent to 6,583.08 in the abbreviated Saturday session.
Turnover was a modest T$35.22 billion.
Electronics shares were hit by profit-taking, falling 0.54 percent. D-Link Corp lost 4.31 percent or T$2.50 to close at T$55.50.

The market had risen by nearly 300 points in early November after the government freed one major state fund to invest in stocks and relaxed the investment cap of another. But the index has hit a strong resistance in the past several sessions.

"The index is not going anywhere if no further good news appears to stimulate trading," said George Hou, fund manager for Jardine Fleming. "Sentiment is stable, so mild profit-taking will hit the market, but not a giant plunge," Hou said.
The heavily weighted financial sector, seen as a central beneficiary of the government liberalisation measures, rose 0.47 percent to support the market.
Chang Hwa, First Commercial and Hua Nan -- Taiwan's "big three" state-run commercial bank -- rose T$1, T$1 and T$0.50 respectively to T$155, T$166 and T$124.50.
Brokers expected the market to continue consolidating in a narrow range on Monday. A 6,550-6,620 range was seen.
